subject: MSA/Order Form — IP indemnity, liability cap carve-out, and escrow remedy
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form - IP indemnity and cap carve-out

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Our legal team circulated redlines this morning to the MSA and Order Form that are holding up procurement. The critical item for us is IP: Acme requires that third-party IP infringement claims be carved out from the monetary liability cap (i.e., the indemnity obligation for IP claims should not be subject to the general cap). They also want reimbursement of defense costs and a right to injunctive relief.

I've attached our redlines (ACME-Requested-Redlines.docx). Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept an IP carve-out, or alternatively whether you would agree to a funded escrow or higher cap specifically for IP claims? We need a clear path to close this week if possible.

Best regards,

Sara Lim
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
Attachment: ACME-Requested-Redlines.docx (docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - IP indemnity and cap carve-out

Hi Sara,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the context. We're aligned that IP claims are sensitive and we want to be reasonable while protecting Redwood from open-ended exposure. High-level proposal from our side:

- Redwood will provide indemnification for third-party IP infringement claims.
- Monetary remedies arising from a covered IP indemnity will be excluded from the general liability cap, but subject to a narrowly scoped mechanism: either (a) a funded escrow equal to 12 months of recurring fees (to be held until resolution), or (b) a supplemental cap equal to 3x the annual contract value, at Acme's election.
- Standard notice-and-cure procedures will apply (we request 30 days to cure where practicable), and Redwood will have the right to control defense with Acme's reasonable participation.
- We also propose a mandatory insurance requirement (commercial liability + IP insurance) and subrogation/right of recovery against third parties.

I attached our suggested redlines (RNW-Proposed-Redlines.docx) that implement the above. Can you confirm which path Acme prefers (escrow vs supplemental cap) and whether Acme is okay with the cure/control language? If you prefer to discuss, I'm available Thursday morning PST for a short call.

Thanks — looping in Karthik and Rishi from legal to help finalize language.

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Contracts & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: RNW-Proposed-Redlines.docx (docx)
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - IP indemnity and cap carve-out

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick proposal — this is helpful. From Acme's perspective the ask is simple: we need IP indemnity to be effectively uncapped. Our risk team cannot accept a cap that could leave Acme on the hook for significant third-party damages even where Redwood's software is alleged to infringe.

That said, we're open to practical mitigations: funded escrow could work if it is large enough and if Redwood agrees to expedited resolution mechanics. We are hesitant about a capped multiple (3x ACV) — historically that's insufficient where patent litigation is involved.

Two quick asks: (1) Can Redwood commit to uncapped indemnity for proven third-party IP claims (subject to standard defenses), and (2) if so, will you accept an escrow sized at one year of fees plus a binding arbitration fast-track for IP disputes? Our procurement lead would like a call Thursday 10:00 AM PST to resolve this.

I've attached our marked PDF so you can see our comments inline (ACME-Redlines-markup.pdf).

Best,

Sara
Attachment: ACME-Redlines-markup.pdf (pdf)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final proposed compromise — IP indemnity and operational controls

Sara, Marissa, Karthik here — following our call earlier today, legal has reviewed and we think there is a workable path that protects both parties and keeps the deal live. Summary of Redwood's final position: 

1) Indemnity: Redwood will indemnify Acme for third-party claims alleging direct infringement of a patent or copyright by Redwood's Service and will cover damages, settlements, and defense costs.

2) Liability treatment: Amounts payable under a covered IP indemnity will not count toward the standard liability cap (i.e., treated outside the cap). This is a concession.

3) Conditioning mechanisms: The uncapped treatment above is conditioned on all of the following operational safeguards:
   - Acme provides prompt written notice and cooperates in the defense;
   - Redwood is granted the right to control the defense and settlement (with Acme's consent required for any settlement that admits liability or imposes non-monetary obligations);
   - Acme must exhaust any third-party remedies first where applicable (subrogation), and Redwood may seek contribution from third parties;
   - Mandatory commercial general liability insurance plus technology/IP insurance with policy limits of at least $5M;
   - A funded escrow equal to 12 months of average monthly recurring revenue (to the extent fees are recurring) will be established as interim security while the claim is resolved.

4) Narrow carveouts: The uncapped treatment applies only to covered third-party IP infringement claims (not to breaches of contract, data breaches, or punitive/consequential damages).

5) Process: We will provide a clean redline implementing this language. If Acme agrees we can route for DocuSign and finalize the MSA + Order Form. DocuSign route here: https://app.docusign.com/remoteSigning?token=ABCD-ACME-1234

Attached is the final compromise redline for your review (Final-Compromise-Redline.docx). Please let us know by end of day tomorrow if this is acceptable; otherwise we can schedule a short follow-up with our C-suite and Acme's procurement.

Regards,

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
